subject: Food Science
title: Glycemic Index
description: A fast breakdown of Glycemic Index for builders.

hook.text: White bread spikes your blood sugar faster than table sugar. The glycemic index measures which foods do this and how much.

buildup.text: GI ranks carbs from 0–100 based on how quickly they raise blood glucose. White bread is 75. An apple is 36. Lentils are 32.

discovery.text: High-GI foods cause rapid insulin spikes, then a crash—leaving you hungry again quickly. Low-GI foods sustain energy for hours.

twist.text: GI only measures single foods eaten alone. Adding fat, protein, or fiber to a meal dramatically lowers the glycemic response.

climax.text: Glycemic load (GL) is more useful—it accounts for portion size. Watermelon has high GI but low GL: little sugar per serving.

punchline.text: GI tells you how fast. GL tells you how much. Both matter for blood sugar.

quiz.question: Why is glycemic load (GL) more useful than glycemic index (GI) alone?
options: GL accounts for portion size—giving a more realistic blood sugar picture
